what_this_is: The Workshop row that runs one SQL statement in the person's own Postgres-wire database and answers its columns and rows, or that database's own error text. It is the PostgreSQL kit's own tool (tools/keep-a-postgres-database-on-a-computer). The connection string is the person's held value, under the name the run gives, handed to the one process on a private pipe (credential_mounts fd 3). The process reaches the database by its address through the run's own proxy, which opens only a host the held value may go to.

payload.label: Run SQL in my database
payload.job: Run one SQL statement in my own database and see its rows
payload.description: Runs exactly one SQL statement as written (sql, with params for $1, $2 and so on), or several in one transaction (statements, ending in a rollback unless then is commit, each behind its own savepoint so a refused one answers its words and the rest still run) in the person's own database, as the login the connection string names: the server refuses text holding more than one command, and a login that may only read (the read connection) cannot write, because the database says so. Give database, the name of one of the person's databases (the computer opens it with the login its vault holds as that name and -connection), or credential_name, the vault name the person saved the connection under (a login that may only read, for a share that may only read), and optionally statement_timeout_ms (how long its statements may run: 120000 ms when absent, at most 598000; the database ends a statement or an open transaction past what is left of the run, so nothing runs on after the run ends). Answers columns, rows and row_count, or the database's own error text. It adds no shape, no list names and no record types. With recipe instead of sql it runs a role recipe (read-data/role-recipes.json, the SQL that makes, grants and takes away a kind of login) as the owner login, in one transaction unless the recipe says otherwise: create with role_credential_name makes that standing login with the password the person holds under that name; create with recipe.valid_until mints a login that stops working then and answers its connection once; drop takes a role away. The connection may name any server that speaks the Postgres wire protocol that this computer reaches on a local port it reports as own-rows-postgres.

credential_name.description: The held name of the connection string: the vault name the person saved it under (a login that may write, or one that may only read).

database.description: The name of one of the person's databases, such as shop_for_who_runs_it. The computer opens it with the login its vault holds as that name and -connection; no caller names a login.

statement_timeout_ms.description: How long the call's statements may run, in milliseconds: 120000 when absent, at most 298000 (the run ends at 300000). The database itself ends a statement or an open transaction past it, less the time the run has used (read-data/time-limits.json).

params.description: The values of $1, $2 and so on.

use.description: The use this statement runs for: a recipe step's declared purpose and surface (config.context.use, set by the workflow engine over any use the step's input carried). Given with database, the computer opens the database with its reader login (one that cannot get round the row rules, change a table or read the use binding) instead of the owner's, and hands the run a ticket of this use that it signed; the statement's transaction claims it first, so the database's row rules read this use and the statement cannot change it. A use with credential_name, which has no ticket, is refused. Absent: the owner's own work, read under the database's own purpose_when_unstated.

purpose.description: The purpose path, such as publish or coach/review.

surface.description: The surface path, such as social/instagram; empty for any surface.

fence.description: With use: the table whose fence to report, as schema.table (or table). The answer then carries fence: {fenced, claimed_purpose, allowed}: whether the table has row rules forced on, the purpose this use claimed (null if none), and whether the login may read it. Given with use only.

role_credential_name.description: A recipe's standing login: the held name of its connection string, whose role and password the recipe makes or drops.

value_credential_name.description: A recipe that takes a held value (may-read-under-row-rules: the database's use key, held as <database>-use-key): the held name of that value, handed to the recipe and filled in by the server, never in the request.

name.description: A recipe of read-data/role-recipes.json (read-only, a share that may only read; own-database, a login and the database it owns, which the login of whoever runs the computer makes).

role.description: The role to drop, or a minted login's name; a standing login's is the held connection's.

valid_until.description: When a minted login (or one made from a password_verifier) stops working, as a time (2026-12-01T00:00:00Z).

limits.description: Per-login limits set when the login is made, each only when given, as the recipe's limits rows say: connection_limit (the most connections this login may hold at once) and statement_timeout_ms (the longest one statement of this login may run). Give the numbers the computer's measured capacity allows; none is chosen here.

password_verifier.description: A login for someone else whose password only they hold: the SCRAM-SHA-256 verifier they made from it (do-work/make-a-login-verifier.mjs on their computer), given with create and role. The database keeps the verifier as the password; the password never comes here and nothing is answered.

table.description: For a recipe that adds rows (may-only-add-rows-for-a-login): the one table whose rows the login may add; given with create and with drop.

columns.description: For a recipe that adds rows, with create: the columns the login may name when it adds a row. A column not listed here and not in fixed cannot be named.

fixed.description: For a recipe that adds rows, with create: column names and the value the server sets on every row the login adds, whatever the login sends (a label every row must carry, a starting status). Not also in columns.

tables.description: For a recipe that grants per table (may-read-under-row-rules), with create or drop: each table the login may read, as schema.table (consent_proof.clip). Each gets SELECT and its schema USAGE, and nothing else in that schema; use_binding may not be named. A table not named here is not granted.

statements.description: Several statements run in one transaction, in order, each behind its own savepoint: one the database refuses answers its words and the rest still run. The answer has one row per statement ({ statement, columns, rows, row_count } or { statement, error }) and refused, how many were refused.

then.description: With statements: how the transaction ends. rollback (when absent) keeps nothing the statements did, so writes are tried and their reads answered without changing the database; commit keeps them.

provenance.source: L078 cart plan section 7.2 (rows in the account owner's Postgres); the client is pg 8.23.1 (MIT) with its pinned dependency tarballs
